status_summary: H.R. 10788, the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act, was introduced in the House on 2026-10-09 and referred to Energy and Commerce, Education and Workforce, and Ways and Means; it would limit the No Surprises Act independent dispute resolution process to services furnished before 2028-01-01 and set later out-of-network payments at a qualifying payment amount recalculated from 2019 contracted rates and indexed to inflation. The bill ends the dispute process the Mandate would scrap but replaces it with a statutory payment benchmark rather than a truth-in-advertising approach that leaves disputes to the parties, so it is recorded as a partial match. The departments continue to run the statutory process: a joint final rule on Federal Independent Dispute Resolution operations, published 2026-06-04 and effective 2026-08-03, revises open negotiation, eligibility review, batching and fees and requires plans to register in the portal. No bill or rule adopting a truth-in-advertising approach was found.

timeline.event: The departments published the final rule Federal Independent Dispute Resolution Operations (91 FR 33900), effective 2026-08-03, which keeps certified IDR entities making payment determinations.

H.R. 10788, the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act, was introduced in the House and referred to three committees; it would end independent dispute resolution for services from 2028 and set payment at a recalculated qualifying payment amount.

title: Replace No Surprises Act arbitration with a truth-in-advertising approach
uncertainties: Checked systematically on 2026-10-18. The Federal Register API check (No Surprises Act with independent dispute resolution, and a variant on surprise billing and arbitration limited to rules and proposed rules) found the 2026-06-04 Federal IDR Operations final rule (2026-11140), which amends and keeps the process, and no document replacing it. The Unified Agenda check was partial: only the Federal Register fallback and the HHS and DOL agenda notices were usable, and they list IDR operations at the final rule stage only. The Congress check, run in review as searches limited to congress.gov and govinfo.gov, found H.R. 10788; its status record and introduced text were read on govinfo, and the trade press account of the same bill is now superseded by the primary record. Other bills seen (H.R. 4710 on balance billing penalties, H.R. 9715 on artificial intelligence in arbitration) were read on their status records and do not replace the process. The agency check covered the CMS No Surprises landing page (modified 2026-09-10), which shows no proposal to end the process. The news check found only the trade account of the same bill. Whether H.R. 10788 counts as a step toward the recommendation is a judgment call: it scraps the dispute process but uses a government payment benchmark, so not_started is also defensible. The IDR operations final rule implements the statute and is treated as context rather than divergence. The final rule's fee amounts and some procedures were not read in full.
